<!-- pr-reviewer: da340c0f2c42b2e65b88038ff228e89750522fe7 -->
**Clean delta: no blockers in this commit.** Ready for the maintainer once its parents land.

**Scope.** This reviews only `881f7726..da340c0f` (one commit, no merge commits in the range). It does not re-review #1615, #1622 or #1634. NeoTech's needs-rework on #1615 still stands and is untouched. Merge order: #1615 -> #1622 -> #1634 -> #1640. No state label is set because of that stack.

**What looks good**
- The loosening is narrow. A stock-source cross drill is now the chain a part-source cross drill drills in the same raw stock: `Solids { source, stock, kept }`, with `kept` the setup's parts (`parts_in_stock`), judged by `cross_part::part_clear` (`cross_spindle.rs`, `generate.rs` ~2061-2072). No new pass-through path found.
- The wall excuse cannot cover a neighbour's wall or a wrong-axis hole. It is the existing measured one (`hole_wall.rs`): a facet is excused only if its sagitta about a declared hole's own axis is <= 0.05 mm, and the excuse is capped by that sagitta. A neighbour's flat wall, or a wall round about some other axis, is part steel. Only a neighbour with a coaxial round hole is excused, which is legal anyway.
- The part-source path is unchanged by construction. `source`, `stock` and `kept` equal the old `facets` / `stock_facets` arguments, and `lathe_reads` still gets `material.facets` when `part_solid`. The existing `drilling_cross*` suites pass unchanged. I did not byte-diff posted NC against main.
- `parts_crossed` stops the vertical-solid law from convicting a declared cross hole's own wall. It is applied in both the 2D tail and the plane-frame arm. `is_cross_drill` joins `is_stock_kept_kind`.
- No `unwrap` / `expect` / `panic!` in the added `src` lines. The decision record is thorough, with readings, dropped options and mutation table. `Changelog:` and `Fixes #1635` are present. Files are within the 400-line habit, except `generate.rs` (3590 lines), which was already far over and grew by about 20.

**Results** (locally, this head only, not merged with main: the PR is stacked and the range is the review; no self-hosted runner was reachable, a 403 on the runners API)
- `stock_source_cross_drill`: 6 passed.
- `drilling_axial` 7, `drilling_cross` 9, `drilling_cross_box` 7, `drilling_cross_holder` 2, `drilling_cross_part` 3, `drilling_cross_spindle` 7, `drilling_cross_stock` 8, `lathe_cross_drill` 5, `keep_law` 7, `neighbour_law` 5, `solid_law` 4, `stock_source_holes` 6, `stock_source_law` 6, `turning_hidden_floor` 6: all passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Mutations re-run by me (each alone, reverted):
  - M2, `kept: &[]` on the stock branch: 3 red (into-part refusal, lathe, MCP), as the author's table says.
  - M4, `is_cross_drill` removed from `is_stock_kept_kind`: 3 red (into-part refusal, lathe, MCP), as the author's table says.

**Requested before merge:** none.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. The pins cover into-part, own-hole, stock-only, faceted wall, no-part, lathe and MCP. None pins a second part whose wall lies on the hole's line, or a hole whose declared axis differs from the modelled hole's. By the code reading above both are refused, but a one-test pin for each would keep that from drifting. A follow-up is fine.
2. The follow-up already named in the PR (a part-source cross drill does not answer to #1621's neighbouring parts) stands as a separate issue.
3. The issue keeps its P1 label while the decision record rates the defect P3 (a false refusal, nothing posted). Re-rating is the maintainer's call.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: da340c0f2c42b2e65b88038ff228e89750522fe7 -->
**Delta clean; no blocker found. Waits for its parents (#1615, #1622, #1634) - not labelled merge-ready.**

Reviewed the delta since 881f7726 only (cross_spindle.rs, generate.rs, keep_law.rs, the new `stock_source_cross_drill.rs` suite, the decision file). The parents have their own reviews.

## What looks good
- The claim holds: on the parent head `part_clear` was handed the stock mesh as the solid to keep, so every stock-source cross drill was refused ("rapids into"). Now the setup's parts are the solid kept and measured, the source stock is the raw material the mouths stand off: the same chain a part-source cross drill drills in that stock.
- Safety direction is right: refuse-everything became the same radial law a part source answers to. A drill into a part where the model has no hole is still refused by name (aligned and turned, bar and box, mill-turn and lathe); a rapid is judged by the same sweep (`RapidInStock`).
- Both directions are pinned. The into-part tests assert the new wording ("cuts into the finished part", "the model has no hole there"), so they fail on the parent head; the legal-hole tests fail there too (refused). Legal chains are compared move for move against the part source's. No existing test is edited or deleted; no unwrap/expect/panic added in src.
- Frames: parts come from `setup_align::parts_facets_in` (the set the program sim judges), the stock is the stock mesh; a stock turned a quarter about Z is pinned and equals the part-source chain.
- Open finding on #1615 (`crates/sim/src/verify/solid.rs:190-195`, a straight rapid up the axis from a cut end is skipped): this delta does not touch solid.rs and does not rely on it. The skip needs a rapid with no stated axis and x, y unchanged; a cross-drill retract runs along a horizontal axis, so it cannot fire here.

## Results (merged with main 22b8fe7a)
On the self-hosted runner: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runs/43568601289 - conclusion success. Quick gate: sim 128 s ok, motion 4 s ok, app 1021 s ok, ui 54 s ok, 4 steps, 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. The run builds the whole stacked PR, so it covers the parents' code too. No `cfg(windows)`/per-OS line in the delta, so no local re-run owed.

## Requested before merge
None.

## Notes (not blocking)
1. Coverage gaps: no test with two parts in the setup, a part marked raw-stock-only, or a rapid/approach that crosses a part (only plunges into steel are pinned).
2. A setup with no part, or whose only model is raw-stock-only or a fixture, keeps nothing and the cross drill passes (`part_clear` returns Ok on an empty mesh). Stated in the decision file and pinned for "no part"; the raw-stock-only case is not pinned. Reasonable (nothing to gouge) but it is the one case with no judgment; a one-line test would settle it.
3. `parts_crossed` skips the 2D tail's solid law for a cross drill. The author says the 3+2 frame arm's guard is not exercised; fine if a cross drill cannot reach it, worth a test if it can.
4. On a lathe with a box stock and no part, the box is still read as the turned work and refused; consistent, unstated.
5. `generate.rs` grows 3572 -> 3590 lines (already far over ~400, flagged not blocking); `job.rs` unchanged.
6. Issue label: the body shows a false refusal, not a pass-through, so P3 is a fair reading of #1635; not relabelled here, the maintainer decides. The closing keyword is truthful if "now judged against the parts" meets the issue's done-means.
7. A comment from the author's own account carrying a reviewer marker does not count as a review; this one is the independent read.

This PR is stacked: #1615 carries an open requested change and #1622, #1634 are unmerged, so it waits for its parents and gets no label from this review.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
